lesson_title: Who Owns the Tavern of the Seas?
hook_text: In 1806, a battle on a beach north of Cape Town decided who would rule the Cape for over a century.
clip_script: The Dutch East India Company is broke. France has invaded the Netherlands. And Britain is worried: the sea route to India runs right past the Cape. In 1795, British warships sail into False Bay and take over. In 1803 the Cape goes back to the Dutch. Then, in January 1806, British troops land at Blaauwberg, win the battle, and stay. Over the next decades, English becomes official, new laws arrive, and settlers push the frontier east into Xhosa land and north across the Orange River. Co-operation and conflict were about to define the frontier.
visual_style: Sailing warships off Table Mountain; a beach battle at Blaauwberg in silhouette; a map with the colony's border sliding east and north.
pacing: Quick political setup, a battle beat, then the map in motion.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on the arrival of the British.
